heading: Timișoara History: 1266 - 1552
text: In 1266, Stephen, King of Hungary, donates the Rety land of Timis to Count Parabuch In 1316, The Hungarian King Charles Robert of Anjou establishes his residence in Timișoara, in a castle built for this purpose, on the site of today's Huniade Castle In 1552, Conquest of the city by the Ottomans. It becomes the capital of the Pashalik of Timișoara

heading: Timișoara History: 1716 - 1728
text: In 1716, Conquest of the city by Habsburg imperial troops led by Prince Eugene of Savoy In 1718, The first and oldest brewery in current day Romania is built here In 1728, Regulating the use of the Bega and Timis rivers. Until 1988, the Bega Canal was the only navigable inland canal in Romania and the first of its kind in south-eastern Europe

heading: Timișoara History: 1771 - 1884
text: In 1771, The first printed newspaper in present-day Romania In 1781, Timișoara becomes a Free Royal City, by a Diploma issued by Emperor Joseph II In 1884, The first city with public electric street lighting in continental Europe. Initially 300 were installed, later the number growing to 731

heading: Timișoara History: 1869 - 1953
text: In 1869, The first horse-drawn tramway in present-day Romania is put into service In 1936, Construction begins on the Metropolitan Cathedral. At 90m tall, it was the tallest church in Romania, until 2018 In 1953, Becomes the only city in Europe with three state theatres in three different languages (Romanian, German, Hungarian) in the same building

heading: Timișoara History: 1989 - 2023
text: In 1989, 16-20.12.1989 The 1989 Anti-Communist Revolution begins; Timișoara proclaims itself the first city free of communism in Romania In 1990, The Timișoara Proclamation, the political programme of the December 1989 Anti-Communist Revolution In 2023, Timișoara is European Culture Capital
